genericProblem: A deterministic generator or frontend consumer starts from a global catalog, a second handwritten source, or an unchecked implementation catalog instead of the owning face-reachable contract closure. The resulting family includes cross-face exports, widened types, stale generated bytes, handwritten runtime keys, generic transport escapes, and wire/implementation disagreement.
finiteDenominator: all non-generated frontend API consumers under both admin apps
all OpenAPI path request, response, parameter, header, error and component references reachable from the 106 operations
searchQueries: enumerate and resolve every operation request, response, parameter, header, error-set and component reference by consumer face
counterexamples: WorkspaceInvitationStatus is a valid public-face DTO dependency under the currently frozen public schema.
WorkspaceOrganizationType is currently reachable by public DTOs; the accepted rename must be applied at the owning contract boundary rather than treated as an arbitrary cross-face leak.
JsonValue is valid in operations-admin because extensionValues consumes it, but it is unreachable from platform-admin and public.
getPublicAssetContent has an accepted multi-page trace exception; this does not permit its response contract to disagree across catalog, OpenAPI path and backend.
The operations-admin operation descriptor set and its reachable component closure were otherwise complete, so the correction must preserve the 56-operation denominator.

findings.problem: Every generated face module exports the global 106-code error vocabulary instead of its reachable face subset.
findings.expected: Exact reachable sets: platform-admin 49, operations-admin 52, public 18.

findings.problem: ACTION_CAPABILITIES and ActionCapabilityKey leak into face wire modules, including platform-admin and public.
findings.expected: Action constants are owned only by the generated operations admin semantic catalog; face wire modules contain wire types and clients only.

findings.problem: JsonValue is emitted into faces from which no reachable component uses it.
findings.expected: Helpers are emitted from the transitive reachable component closure only.

findings.problem: The two generated admin catalogs have asymmetric and over-broad semantics: operations UX metadata is incomplete while platform contains operations actions.
findings.expected: Each catalog is face-owned and exactly generated from admin-catalog.json, including the 17 operations UX definitions.

findings.problem: Business features import action constants from generated wire modules instead of the operations semantic catalog.
findings.expected: All feature authorization comparisons consume generated semantic keys from one owning catalog.

findings.problem: Page and action key schemas are repeated inline or widened to string, so generated consumers cannot retain a closed-set type.
findings.expected: Reusable PageDesignKey and ActionCapabilityKey projections are generated from the owning catalog and referenced by all wire schemas.

findings.problem: Problem.errorCode remains an arbitrary string and transport feedback can expose untrusted server detail.
findings.expected: Face-reachable generated error semantics are closed-set and user feedback uses an approved safe mapping.

findings.problem: Generic request<unknown> transports accept handwritten operationId strings and cast responses, bypassing generated request/response and header semantics.
findings.expected: Features call generated per-operation typed clients only; no generic transport escape remains.

findings.problem: App API files retain duplicate handwritten base endpoints for currentSession and workspaceSessionEntry.
findings.expected: The generated operation surface is the sole endpoint source.

findings.problem: Legacy src/main.js files retain raw fetch and manually written endpoints outside the typed app architecture.
findings.expected: No executable or admitted frontend source bypasses generated transport.

findings.problem: The generator trusts implementation-catalog request/response names without resolving and comparing the owning OpenAPI path; getPublicAssetContent currently disagrees as BinaryAssetContent versus PublicAssetReference.
findings.expected: Generation fails closed on path/catalog disagreement and preserves the accepted URL-bearing public asset response.

findings.problem: The accepted WorkspaceOrganizationType to ServiceNodeType rename is not consistently reflected at the owning contract boundary.
findings.expected: The rename is applied once at the owning schema and propagated by generation without reviving deprecated semantics.

findings.problem: Path parameter TypeScript types are hardcoded as string or number instead of being derived from OpenAPI parameter schemas.
findings.expected: Every generated path parameter type is resolved from the owning path contract.

findings.problem: Required Idempotency-Key semantics are absent from generated clients while generic transports allow arbitrary optional headers for every operation.
findings.expected: Required and forbidden header shapes are generated per operation.

findings.problem: Generated operation-id type names use malformed face casing such as operationsadminOperationId.
findings.expected: Stable exported identifiers use PlatformAdminOperationId, OperationsAdminOperationId and PublicOperationId.

findings.problem: Runtime operation descriptors expose trace-only pseudo page namespaces that are not members of the 25 pageDesignKey denominator.
findings.expected: Trace metadata stays in trace catalogs; runtime semantic bindings use only the approved admin page catalog and explicit shared-operation exceptions.

findings.problem: A global schema-name fallback can silently resolve an invalid relative reference or cross-face component.
findings.expected: All component references resolve exactly from their declared relative target and unresolved references fail closed.

findings.problem: Static navigation Chinese labels can be duplicated between generated catalog and session projection, allowing two sources of UI truth.
findings.expected: Admin catalog owns static labels; session data carries authorization projection and keys only.

findings.problem: Deterministic generator writes can bypass file-level hook receipts, allowing generated output to drift or become unaccounted even when a final check exists.
findings.expected: Every deterministic generation command snapshots exact admitted outputs and emits pre/post receipts through the existing compliance control.
